title: Entire's Git Forge Rethinks Git Collaboration for Coding Agents
gist: Entire, led by former GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke, is a Git forge built for human-agent collaboration that replaces PR timelines with 'trails' showing repeatedly-run eval scores and gated merges, plus open-source 'continuous memory' tools. It claims pushes up to 89x faster than GitHub and joins a crowded field of agent-era source control entrants.

insights.claim: Entire's premise is that the pull request model of traditional development infrastructure is ill-suited to AI agents that generate, review and iterate on code at high speed.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Signals a potential platform shift threatening GitHub/GitLab's core collaboration workflow.
insights.locator: Entire is a Git forge designed

insights.claim: Thomas Dohmke, former GitHub CEO and now Entire CEO, frames GitHub and GitLab as centered on human asynchronous code review, while a multi-agent forge centers on asynchronous orchestration, versioning and auditing of AI agents alongside humans.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: A former GitHub CEO betting against the PR model gives the thesis credibility and competitive edge.
insights.locator: As Thomas Dohmke, former GitHub CEO

insights.claim: Entire argues the pull request timeline has become an audit log only the agent reads and no longer gives developers the information to merge with confidence.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Merge-confidence tooling, not code generation, may be the bottleneck and value pool in agentic coding.
insights.quote: The pull request [timeline] has become an audit log that only the agent reads. It does not provide the information for the developer to decide whether they can merge with confidence.
insights.locator: Built on top of a fully distributed

insights.claim: Entire claims its fully distributed architecture enables pushes up to 89 times faster than GitHub.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Vendor performance claim aimed at high-frequency agent push workloads; unverified.
insights.locator: Built on top of a fully distributed

insights.claim: Entire's trails surface eval scores updated on every push, with a cloud-sandboxed review agent scoring code quality, security, 'slop' and whether human review is required, plus a rationale.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Automated agent-on-agent review with scoring is emerging as a product category.

insights.claim: Entire shows the last five runs plus the current run for each eval because it believes one-shot agent loops often miss critical issues and that repeating loops until scores stabilize is crucial for agentic coding success.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Implies agentic coding consumes multiple review iterations per change, multiplying compute/token demand.
insights.quote: one-shot loops are often missing a critical issue. Repeating the loops and stabilizing the scores is crucial for the success of agentic coding.
insights.locator: The last 5 runs and the current run

insights.claim: In Entire, all review-agent findings must be resolved or closed before merge, and repositories can define Gates specifying approval conditions; merges should happen only when confidence is high, risk low and findings cleared.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Governance gates are a likely enterprise selling point for agent-written code.
insights.quote: Only when the confidence is high, risk is low, and all findings are cleared, the merge should happen.

insights.claim: Entire's continuous memory preserves accumulated repository knowledge for reuse across agent sessions via two open-source tools: entire-graph, a precomputed repo map with ranked code search, definitions and callers, and entire-brain, a persistent memory layer combining that map with prior agent sessions and Git history.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Context/memory layers for agents are a contested infrastructure layer; open-sourcing it is a distribution play.
insights.locator: Another foundational concept introduced by Entire

insights.claim: An Entire employee argues the core problem is not languages or tools but that reasoning gets lost between person and artifact, and that agents made this acute because no one remembers why code exists.
insights.speaker: Haimantika
insights.so_what: Positions provenance/'why' capture as the durable value in agent-era source control.
insights.quote: Agents just made that acute, because now there's no one who remembers. That's the bit we're trying to fix.
insights.locator: Commenting on the announcement on Hacker News

insights.claim: A Hacker News commenter contends engineers delegated coding to agents because programming languages and tools leave much to be desired.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Alternative view that better languages, not new forges, could address the problem.
insights.locator: Commenting on the announcement on Hacker News

insights.claim: Entire is one of several new source code management entrants alongside Zed DeltaDB, Anthropic Scion, East River Source Control, Cursor Origin and Radicle.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Many well-funded players targeting the forge layer suggests GitHub's position is being actively contested.
insights.locator: Entire is only one of several

insights.claim: Entire integrates with CI platforms such as Buildkite and Depot.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Ecosystem integrations reduce switching costs away from GitHub.
insights.locator: As a final note on Entire
